subject: Radiant Retail: Checkout p99 spikes impacting throughput — urgent mitigation & exec update
messages:
From: Elaine Wong <elaine@radiantretail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 22:05:18 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Checkout timeouts & p99 spikes during 6-9pm PST window

Naomi —

We started seeing severe checkout problems around 21:45 PST. Key symptoms:
- p50 unchanged (~120ms) but p99 jumped from ~1.2s to 14s for generate endpoint.
- Error rate increased from 0.3% to ~3.7% (5xx and 429s).
- Overall throughput to the Redwood endpoint dropped by ~30% during the spike.

Customer impact: ~6% of checkout attempts timed out (user-facing failures). This is hitting our peak traffic as we ramp promotions. Attached logs show sample request ids and stack traces; Grafana link below has the timeline.

We suspect some sort of queueing/backpressure in your serving tier — several requests appear to queue for >10s before a 503 or 200 with huge latency. Can you confirm? We need an immediate mitigation path and an ETA.

Sample request id: rr-checkout-20280210-22-1a9f
Grafana: https://grafana.radiantretail.com/d/rr-checkout/checkout-traces

Thanks — Elaine

Forwarding Elaine's note — Radiant is seeing large p99 tails and increased 5xx/429s during their evening peak. Elaine included logs and a Grafana link (attached).

Immediate asks:
- Can infra triage whether this is KV cache thrash / scheduling queueing / concurrency cap on prod pool?
- Quick mitigation options: route Radiant to dedicated capacity, temporarily lower concurrency per-request, enable prefix KV caching, or apply short-term rate limiting on noisy routes.
- I'll take point on external comms — Markus/Marissa, recommend we prepare an executive note and offer short-term credits if appropriate.

Please reply with proposed short-term mitigation (0–2h) and a plan for 24h follow-up.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: Checkout timeouts & p99 spikes during 6-9pm PST window

Quick triage notes (initial 20m):
- Observed host pool grb-prod-11 showing sustained concurrency hits at the pool level starting 21:40 PST. Concurrent inflight requests per host peaked at configured cap (64).
- KV-cache miss-rate went from ~6% to ~42% across requests for Radiant; this caused repeated model re-evaluations and increased token compute time.
- A subset of requests received 429 from our internal scheduler while queues grew; those either retried or fell through to 503.

Immediate mitigation (can be done in 15–30m):
1) Route Radiant to dedicated pool ded-prod-rr (has spare headroom) — quick config flip.
2) Bump concurrency cap on grb-prod-11 from 64 -> 80 as emergency (short window).
3) Enable prefix KV caching for Radiant's checkout route to reduce repeated KV thrash.
4) Short-term client-side advisory: ask Radiant to enable exponential backoff for retries (I can provide suggested headers).

I'll own 1–3 and coordinate with ops to apply. After we stabilize, we should run a forced warmup of the KV cache and follow with a root-cause postmortem.

ETA: routing + cache flip: ~20m. Concurrency bump: ~10m. I'll post status updates to this thread.

— Karthik
